mainTopic: Sisters of a חלוצה, divorcée, or יבמה who fall to יבום; whether a יבמה forbidden for a time becomes permitted again; and the three-month wait before remarriage
overview:
The amud opens by finishing an earlier question. The Rabbis forbade the צרה of a חלוצה's relative, because a relative comes to court with the חלוצה and people could mix them up. A צרה never comes along, so her relatives were not forbidden.
A new משנה then teaches that a חלוצה's sister who falls to the same יבם needs חליצה. A divorcée's sister is fully exempt. ריש לקיש explains why: the first is forbidden only מדרבנן, the second מדאורייתא.
The משנה also says that a brother who betrothed the sister of a שומרת יבם must wait until the יבמה is freed, and שמואל rules this way.
The גמרא then asks: if the betrothed wife dies, may he do יבום with her sister? רב and רבי חנינא say yes. שמואל and רב אסי say no.
רבא explains רב: a יבמה who was permitted, then forbidden, then permitted again returns to her first permission. רב המנונא challenges this from a ברייתא. רבא answers that the ברייתא follows רבי אלעזר, and the גמרא shows that even רבנן could agree with שמואל, since the ban began after נפילה.
Finally, a new משנה requires a three-month wait before a יבמה or any woman remarries. רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי give exceptions, and רבי יוסי's reason continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A relative goes with her to court, a co-wife does not
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the difference between the two cases. The relative of a חלוצה goes with her to court, so the Rabbis made a decree about that relative's co-wife. The co-wife of a חלוצה does not go with her to court, so the Rabbis made no decree about her relatives.
steps.simpleTranslation: That woman (the relative) goes along with her to court, so the Rabbis decreed about them. This woman (the co-wife) does not go along with her to court, so the Rabbis did not decree about them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is answering a question asked just before this. Why is the צרה of a חלוצה's relative forbidden, while the relatives of a חלוצה's צרה are permitted? The answer depends on who usually comes to court with the חלוצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חלוצה's sister or other relative often comes to court with her for the חליצה. People might think the relative was the one who did חליצה. If the יבם then married that relative's צרה, people might wrongly think a חלוצה's צרה is permitted, so the Rabbis forbade it. A צרה never comes along, so nobody will mix her up with the חלוצה, and there was no reason to forbid her relatives.

keyTerms.meaning: the court, where חליצה is done
the Rabbis made a protective decree (גזירה)
a co-wife, another wife of the same husband
a woman who has gone through חליצה

steps.whatToRemember: A rabbinic decree (גזירה) here depends on whether people could realistically confuse the two women. The relative comes to court and could be confused with the חלוצה, so there is a decree. The צרה does not come, so there is no decree.
steps.confusionAlert: Keep the two cases straight. 'הך' is the relative of the חלוצה, and its צרה is forbidden. 'האי' is the צרה of the חלוצה, and its relatives are permitted.

phrases.english: That one, who goes together with her to court
phrases.notes: 'That one' is the relative of the חלוצה, who often comes along to the חליצה.

phrases.english: the Rabbis decreed regarding them.

phrases.aramaic: הַאי דְּלָא אָזְלָא בַּהֲדַהּ לְבֵי דִּינָא
phrases.english: This one, who does not go together with her to court
phrases.notes: 'This one' is the צרה (co-wife) of the חלוצה.

phrases.english: the Rabbis did not decree regarding them.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָךְ דְּאָזְלָא בַּהֲדַהּ לְבֵי דִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers a question from the previous section about the difference between the two rabbinic rules
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction based on what people actually see (who comes to court)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both cases look the same, so both should be forbidden or both permitted.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the woman who comes to court could be confused with the חלוצה, so only her case needed a decree.

steps.title: Brother marries the sister of a חלוצה and dies
steps.stepSummary: A man did חליצה with his יבמה. Then his brother married her sister and died. The sister must do חליצה with him but may not do יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: One who did חליצה with his יבמה, and then his brother married her sister and died: she does חליצה but does not do יבום.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. Its first case is a woman who falls to יבום before a man whose former חלוצה is her sister.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Marrying the sister of one's חלוצה is forbidden, so יבום is not possible. Still, she is not released without חליצה. This prohibition comes from the Rabbis, so by Torah law the יבום bond is still there and only חליצה can end it.

keyTerms.meaning: short for מתניתין, 'our משנה', marking the start of a new משנה
his יבמה, his brother's widow who falls to him

phrases.english: Mishnah:
One who performed חליצה with his יבמה
and his brother married her sister
and died —
phrases.notes: The brother who married the sister died with no children, so his widow now falls to the man who did the first חליצה.

phrases.english: she performs חליצה but does not enter into יבום.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַחוֹלֵץ לִיבִמְתּוֹ וְנָשָׂא אָחִיו אֶת אֲחוֹתָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The sister of one's חלוצה who falls to him for יבום must do חליצה, not יבום.

steps.title: Brother marries the sister of a divorcée and dies
steps.stepSummary: A man divorced his wife. Then his brother married her sister and died. That sister is fully exempt from both יבום and חליצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And similarly, one who divorced his wife, and his brother married her sister and died: she is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a parallel case, this time with a divorced wife in place of a חלוצה. The result is different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sister of one's divorcée is forbidden by Torah law (אחות גרושתו). That makes her an ערוה to him, so the יבום bond never applies to her at all. That is why she needs no חליצה. In the case of step 2, the prohibition was only from the Rabbis, so she still needed חליצה.

keyTerms.meaning: exempt from both חליצה and יבום
the sister of his divorced wife, forbidden by the Torah while the divorcée is alive

steps.confusionAlert: 'וכן' (similarly) does not mean the result is the same. In step 2 she needs חליצה. Here she is completely exempt.

phrases.english: And similarly, one who divorces his wife
and his brother married her sister and died —
this woman is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן הַמְגָרֵשׁ אֶת אִשְׁתּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel case that gives a stronger result: full exemption
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The sister of one's divorcée who falls to him is exempt from both יבום and חליצה.

steps.title: Betrothing the sister of a שומרת יבם — wait
steps.stepSummary: A widow is waiting for יבום (a שומרת יבם), and one of the brothers betrothed her sister. In the name of רבי יהודה בן בתירא they said that this brother must wait until another brother does an act with the יבמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A woman waiting for her יבם, whose sister was betrothed by one of the brothers: in the name of רבי יהודה בן בתירא they said, we tell him: wait until your brother performs an act.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves to a new case. Here the brother's link to the יבמה is only a זיקה (a waiting bond). Nobody has done יבום or חליצה yet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While the יבמה waits, each brother is bound to her by זיקה. Marrying the sister of a woman he is bound to is forbidden. So the betrothal stays in place, but he may not marry and live with his betrothed until another brother does חליצה or יבום and ends his bond.

keyTerms.meaning: a widow waiting for יבום or חליצה
an act, meaning חליצה or יבום

phrases.english: A woman waiting for her יבם
whose sister the brother of the יבם betrothed —

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתִירָא אָמְרוּ
phrases.english: in the name of רבי יהודה בן בתירא they said:
We say to him:
Wait until your brother performs an act.

steps.triggerLanguage: שׁוֹמֶרֶת יָבָם שֶׁקִּידֵּשׁ אָחִיו אֶת אֲחוֹתָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from completed חליצה or divorce to an unresolved זיקה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A brother who betrothed the sister of a שומרת יבם may not marry her until another brother does חליצה or יבום.

steps.title: When the bond ends, he may marry his betrothed
steps.stepSummary: If another brother did חליצה or יבום with the יבמה, or if the יבמה died, the betrothing brother may now marry his betrothed.
steps.simpleTranslation: If his brother did חליצה with her or married her, he may marry his wife. If the יבמה died, he may marry his wife.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה explains what ends the waiting period from step 4. These are the good outcomes, where the problem simply goes away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If another brother does חליצה or יבום, the זיקה to the remaining brothers ends. If the יבמה dies, the bond ends as well. In both cases his betrothed is no longer the sister of a woman bound to him, so he may complete the marriage.

keyTerms.meaning: he may take her in, completing the marriage (נישואין)
the widow who falls to יבום

phrases.english: If his brother performed חליצה with her or married her
he may take in his wife.
phrases.notes: 'His wife' is the sister he had only betrothed until now.

phrases.english: If the יבמה died
he may take in his wife.

steps.triggerLanguage: חָלַץ לָהּ אָחִיו אוֹ כְּנָסָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the outcomes that end the waiting period of step 4
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Once the זיקה ends, through another brother's act or the יבמה's death, he may marry his betrothed.

steps.title: If the other יבם dies, he loses both women
steps.stepSummary: If the other יבם dies before ending the bond, the betrothing brother must divorce his betrothed with a גט and release the יבמה with חליצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the יבם died, he must send away his wife with a גט, and his brother's wife with חליצה.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the bad outcome. The brother who was supposed to act dies, and now the betrothing brother is the only one left bound to the יבמה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His betrothed is the sister of a woman bound to him, so he must divorce her with a גט. After that, the יבמה is the sister of his divorcée, so he cannot do יבום with her. Since the bond to her started before the divorce, she still needs חליצה. He ends up losing both women.
steps.whatToRemember: A זיקה alone is strong enough to block marriage to the יבמה's sister. If he is left as the only יבם, he must give a גט to his betrothed and do חליצה with the יבמה.
steps.confusionAlert: Here 'his wife' is the betrothed sister, and 'his brother's wife' is the יבמה. One gets a גט, the other gets חליצה.

phrases.english: If the יבם died
he must send away his wife with a bill of divorce
and his brother's wife with חליצה.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵת יָבָם יוֹצִיא אֶת אִשְׁתּוֹ בְּגֵט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The opposite outcome to step 5, where the bond is never ended by another brother
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the other יבם dies, the betrothing brother must divorce his betrothed and do חליצה with the יבמה.

steps.title: Why does the משנה say 'and similarly'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה links the divorce case to the חליצה case with 'וכן' when their rulings are different.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What does 'and similarly' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges one word in the משנה. It is setting up a quick fix in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the חליצה case the sister still needs חליצה (step 2). In the divorce case she is fully exempt (step 3). 'וכן' suggests the two cases are the same, but they are not.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
What is / what does it mean
And similarly, meaning the same rule applies

phrases.english: GEMARA: What is 'and similarly'?
phrases.notes: The משנה used this word to join the divorce case to the חליצה case, but they end with different rulings.

steps.triggerLanguage: מאי וכן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the משנה to the גמרא and questions the משנה's wording linking steps 2 and 3.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'Similarly' implies the same ruling, but one case needs חליצה and the other is fully exempt.

steps.title: Read it as 'but one who divorces'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא fixes the wording: read 'אבל המגרש' instead of 'וכן'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say instead: 'But one who divorces.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by changing the word 'and similarly' to 'but', which shows the second case is different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With 'אבל', the משנה now clearly contrasts the two cases. The divorce case gets a lighter outcome: no חליצה at all.

phrases.english: Say: 'But one who divorces.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אימא אבל המגרש
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changing the wording of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'וכן' would mean the divorce case has the same ruling as the חליצה case.
steps.terutzMaskana: The word should be 'אבל', showing that the divorce case has a different ruling.

steps.title: A divorcee's sister is forbidden by Torah law, a חלוצה's sister by rabbinic law
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש explains the difference: a גרושה's sister is forbidden מדאורייתא, and a חלוצה's sister only מדרבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: Here רבי taught that a divorcee's sister is forbidden by Torah law, and a חלוצה's sister is forbidden by rabbinic law.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש explains why the two cases end differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A divorced wife's sister is forbidden by the Torah, so the יבום bond never takes hold and she is fully exempt. A חלוצה's sister is forbidden only by the Rabbis, so the Torah's bond still exists and she needs חליצה to be freed.

keyTerms.meaning: The sister of one's divorced wife
The sister of a woman one did חליצה with

steps.whatToRemember: A גרושה's sister is forbidden מדאורייתא, so there is no יבום and no חליצה. A חלוצה's sister is forbidden only מדרבנן, so she needs חליצה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains the משנה's two rulings. A Torah-level ban removes the יבום bond completely, while a rabbinic ban leaves the bond in place.

phrases.english: ריש לקיש said,
Here רבי taught:
phrases.notes: 'רבי' is רבי יהודה הנשיא, who arranged the משנה.

phrases.english: a divorcee's sister is forbidden by Torah law,
a חלוצה's sister is forbidden by rabbinic law.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר ריש לקיש כאן שנה רבי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason behind the contrast set up in step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The sister of a גרושה is forbidden מדאורייתא, so she is fully exempt. The sister of a חלוצה is forbidden מדרבנן, so she needs חליצה.

steps.title: The הלכה follows רבי יהודה בן בתירא
steps.stepSummary: Back on the משנה's case of שומרת יבם, שמואל rules like רבי יהודה בן בתירא.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'A שומרת יבם whose sister was betrothed by a brother, and so on.' שמואל said: The הלכה follows רבי יהודה בן בתירא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next part of the משנה and gives שמואל's practical ruling on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This confirms in practice the rule from steps 4-6. The brother who betrothed the sister must wait until another brother frees the יבמה.

keyTerms.meaning: The halacha follows the words of

phrases.english: 'A widow waiting for her יבם, where he betrothed,' etc.
שמואל said:

phrases.aramaic: הֲלָכָה כְּדִבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתֵירָא.
phrases.english: The halacha follows the words of רבי יהודה בן בתירא.

steps.triggerLanguage: שומרת יבם שקידש וכו׳ אמר שמואל הלכה כדברי רבי יהודה בן בתירא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next section of the משנה and gives a practical ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The halacha follows רבי יהודה בן בתירא: the betrothing brother must wait until the יבמה is freed.

steps.title: If his wife died, may he do יבום with her sister?
steps.stepSummary: The Sages ask: the יבמה was forbidden to the יבם as his wife's sister. If his wife dies, may he now do יבום with her?
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: If his wife died, what is the law about his יבמה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new question. It is setting up a disagreement that comes in the next two steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The יבמה is his wife's sister, so she is forbidden to him while his wife is alive. In this case the betrothal happened after the יבמה had already fallen to him, so she was permitted at first and only became forbidden later. The question is whether the ban disappears once the wife dies, or whether it stays.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked among the Sages

phrases.english: It was asked of them:
If his wife died, what is the law about his יבמה?
phrases.notes: His wife is the יבמה's sister, and that is why the יבמה was forbidden to him until now.

steps.triggerLanguage: איבעיא להו מתה אשתו מהו ביבמתו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the topic of a יבמה who is a wife's sister and asks about a new case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Once the wife who caused the ban has died, is the יבם allowed to do יבום with her sister?

steps.title: רב and רבי חנינא: he is permitted
steps.stepSummary: רב and רבי חנינא both say that once his wife dies, he may do יבום with the יבמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב and רבי חנינא both say: If his wife died, he is permitted to his יבמה.
steps.whatsHappening: The first opinion answers the question: yes, he is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this view, the ban depended only on his wife being alive. Once she dies, the reason for the ban is gone, so the יבום may go ahead.

phrases.english: רב and רבי חנינא, who both say:
If his wife died, he is permitted to his יבמה.

steps.triggerLanguage: רב ורבי חנינא דאמרי תרוייהו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first answer to the question in step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He is permitted to do יבום once his wife has died.

steps.title: שמואל and רב אסי: he is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: שמואל and רב אסי both say that even after his wife dies, he remains forbidden to the יבמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל and רב אסי both say: If his wife died, he is forbidden to his יבמה.
steps.whatsHappening: The opposing opinion answers the question: no, he is still forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this view, the ban does not simply disappear when the wife dies. The יבמה was permitted when she fell to him, but became forbidden once he betrothed her sister. Having been forbidden after she fell to him, she stays forbidden for יבום even after the wife dies.
steps.whatToRemember: There is a disagreement. רב and רבי חנינא say the death of the wife permits the יבמה. שמואל and רב אסי say she stays forbidden.

phrases.english: שמואל and רב אסי, who both say:
If his wife died, he is forbidden to his יבמה.

steps.triggerLanguage: שמואל ורב אסי דאמרי תרוייהו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite answer to step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He stays forbidden to the יבמה even after his wife dies.

steps.title: רבא Explains רב's Reasoning
steps.stepSummary: רבא says רב's reason is that the יבמה was permitted, became forbidden, and became permitted again, so she returns to her original permission for יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: What is רב's reason? She is a יבמה who was permitted, then forbidden, then permitted again. So she should go back to her first permitted status.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the reason behind רב's ruling in Step 12 that the יבם may do יבום once his wife dies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the brother died, the יבמה was permitted to the יבם. She became forbidden because he was married to her sister. Once his wife died, that problem disappeared. רבא says the original permission for יבום simply comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: She was permitted and then became forbidden
She went back and became permitted again

steps.whyThisMatters: This principle, permitted, forbidden, then permitted again, is exactly what רב המנונא will now test against a ברייתא.

phrases.english: Rava said: What is Rav's reason?
Because she is a yevama
who was permitted and then became forbidden,
phrases.notes: She was permitted when her husband died. She became forbidden because the יבם was married to her sister.

phrases.english: and then went back and was permitted,
so she should return to her first permitted status.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind רב's position from Step 12, which stands against שמואל's view in Step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A יבמה who was permitted, then forbidden, then permitted again returns to her original permission for יבום.

steps.title: רב המנונא Quotes a Case of Three Brothers
steps.stepSummary: רב המנונא quotes a ברייתא. Two brothers are married to two sisters, and a third brother is unmarried. In the end, the first widow may only do חליצה, not יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב המנונא objected: There are three brothers. Two are married to two sisters, and one is unmarried. One of the sisters' husbands died, and the unmarried brother did מאמר with his widow. Then the second brother died. Then the second brother's wife died too. That first יבמה does חליצה and not יבום.
steps.whatsHappening: רב המנונא quotes a ברייתא to challenge רבא's explanation of רב. This step sets up the case, and the next step spells out the attack.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the first brother died, his widow was permitted to the unmarried brother. When the second brother died, the unmarried brother became bound to both sisters, so the first widow became forbidden. When the second widow died, the problem went away, yet the ברייתא still says only חליצה.

keyTerms.meaning: A form of betrothal done with a יבמה before יבום
She does חליצה but not יבום

steps.confusionAlert: In this case the second sister is not the unmarried brother's wife. She is only bound to him as a second יבמה, through זיקה. That bond is what made her sister forbidden to him for a while.

phrases.english: Rav Hamnuna raised an objection:
Three brothers,
two are married to two sisters,
and one is unmarried.
One of the sisters' husbands died,
and the unmarried brother did a מאמר with her,
and afterward his second brother died,
phrases.notes: Now the second widow also falls to the unmarried brother, and she is the first widow's sister.

phrases.english: and afterward his wife died after him,
phrases.notes: This is the second brother's wife, who died after her husband.

phrases.english: that yevama does חליצה and does not do יבום.
phrases.notes: "That יבמה" means the first brother's widow.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵתִיב רַב הַמְנוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that seems to contradict the principle רבא just stated.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's explanation of רב: permitted, forbidden, then permitted again returns to the first permission.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא's case follows the same pattern, yet it forbids יבום.

steps.title: Why Doesn't She Return to Her First Permission?
steps.stepSummary: רב המנונא asks: in the ברייתא's case, why shouldn't the יבמה go back to her first permission, just as רב says?
steps.simpleTranslation: But why? Let her be like a יבמה who was permitted, then forbidden, then permitted again. She should return to her first permitted status!
steps.whatsHappening: רב המנונא spells out his challenge. The ברייתא's יבמה fits רבא's principle exactly, yet she is not allowed יבום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's case has the same three stages as רב's case: permitted, forbidden, permitted again. Since the ברייתא still forbids יבום, it seems the original permission does not come back. That goes against רבא's explanation of רב.

keyTerms.meaning: Let her be, she should be treated as

phrases.english: But why?
Let her be like a yevama who was permitted
and became forbidden, and then was permitted again,
she should return to her first permitted status!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַמַּאי? תֶּיהְוֵי כִּיבָמָה שֶׁהוּתְּרָה וְנֶאֶסְרָה וְחָזְרָה וְהוּתְּרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the challenge out of the ברייתא quoted in Step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's principle that a יבמה who was permitted, forbidden, and permitted again returns to her original permission.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא's case has the same three stages, yet it rules 'חליצה, not יבום'. So the original permission does not return.

steps.title: רבא's late answer: the ברייתא follows רבי אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: רבא was silent at first. After רב המנונא left, רבא said the ברייתא follows רבי אלעזר, who holds that a יבמה forbidden even for one moment stays forbidden forever.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא was silent. After רב המנונא left, רבא said to himself: Why didn't you tell him that this ברייתא follows רבי אלעזר? רבי אלעזר says that once she stood forbidden to the יבם for one moment, she is forbidden to him forever.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא had no answer while רב המנונא was there. Afterward he thinks of one: the ברייתא follows רבי אלעזר, not everyone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said the יבמה may only do חליצה, and that seemed to argue against רב. רבא answers that this ruling comes from רבי אלעזר's special view: one moment of being forbidden makes her forbidden forever. So רב can follow the other חכמים, who disagree with רבי אלעזר.

keyTerms.meaning: He was silent (he had no answer)
One moment in a forbidden state

steps.confusionAlert: When רבא says 'Why didn't you tell him,' he is talking to himself. There is no second person here.

phrases.english: He was silent.
phrases.notes: This is רבא, who could not answer רב המנונא right away.

phrases.english: After he left, he said:
Why did you not say to him,
phrases.notes: רבא is speaking to himself here.

phrases.english: It is the view of Rabbi Elazar,
who said: Once she stood before him
for one moment in a forbidden state
she is forbidden to him forever?

steps.triggerLanguage: אמאי לא אמרת ליה רבי אלעזר היא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב המנונא's challenge from Step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributes the challenging ברייתא to a single תנא (רבי אלעזר) whom רב does not have to follow.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to be everyone's view, so it would argue against רב.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is only רבי אלעזר's view, so רב can disagree with it.

steps.title: רבא doubts his own answer
steps.stepSummary: רבא questions his own answer. Maybe רבי אלעזר only said 'forbidden forever' when she was unfit from the moment she fell to the יבם, and not when she was fit at first.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then he said: Maybe רבי אלעזר only said this where she was not fit for him at the time she fell to him. But where she was fit at that time, did he really say it?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא now pokes a hole in his own answer. He is not sure that רבי אלעזר's rule fits the case in the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי אלעזר's known case, she was forbidden right from the start. In the ברייתא's case, she was fit when her husband died and only became forbidden later, when the יבם married her sister. So maybe רבי אלעזר would agree that she becomes permitted again here. If so, the ברייתא is everyone's view, and the challenge to רב comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: Then he said (he went back and said)
The time of 'falling,' the moment she becomes tied to the יבם

phrases.english: Then he said:
One could say that Rabbi Elazar said it
where she was not fit at the time of falling,
phrases.notes: 'Falling' means the moment her husband dies and she becomes tied to the יבם.

phrases.english: but where she was fit at the time of falling,
did he say it?

steps.triggerLanguage: הדר אמר אימור דאמר רבי אלעזר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's own answer from Step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's answer that the ברייתא follows רבי אלעזר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי אלעזר's rule may only apply when she was unfit from the start. In the ברייתא she was fit at first, so his rule may not apply.

steps.title: A ברייתא proves רבי אלעזר rules this way even here
steps.stepSummary: רבא brings a ברייתא showing that רבי אלעזר rules this way in our exact case, where the יבם married the יבמה's sister. If the wife dies, the יבמה only does חליצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then he said: Yes, he does say it. For it was taught: רבי אלעזר says, if his יבמה dies, he is permitted to his wife. If his wife dies, that יבמה does חליצה and may not do יבום.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers his own doubt. A ברייתא shows that רבי אלעזר keeps her forbidden even when she was fit at first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ברייתא deals with our case, where she was fit at first and became forbidden later. רבי אלעזר still says that after the wife dies, the יבמה may only do חליצה. So רב המנונא's ברייתא can be the view of רבי אלעזר alone, and רבא's answer for רב works again.
steps.whatToRemember: The ruling that the יבמה only does חליצה belongs to רבי אלעזר. He says this even when she was fit at first, so רב can follow the חכמים who disagree.

phrases.english: Then he said: Yes,
for it was taught: Rabbi Elazar says:
If his יבמה died, he is permitted to his wife,
if his wife died,
that יבמה does חליצה and does not do יבום.

steps.triggerLanguage: הדר אמר אין והתניא רבי אלעזר אומר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the doubt from Step 18 and confirms the answer from Step 17.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אלעזר holds that she stays forbidden even when she was fit at the time of falling.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא quoting רבי אלעזר on a יבם who married the יבמה's sister.

steps.title: Do שמואל and רב אסי follow רבי אלעזר?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that שמואל and רב אסי, who keep the יבמה forbidden, are simply following רבי אלעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say that שמואל and רב אסי, who say she stays forbidden, hold like רבי אלעזר?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It suggests that the argument between רב and שמואל matches the argument between רבי אלעזר and the חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We just learned that רבי אלעזר keeps the יבמה forbidden in this case. שמואל and רב אסי rule the same way, so maybe they are just following him. The word 'לימא' tells us this is only a suggestion, and the גמרא will look at whether it is correct.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? (a suggestion the גמרא will test)

phrases.english: Shall we say that Shmuel and Rav Asi,
who say this, hold like Rabbi Elazar?
phrases.notes: They are the ones from Step 13 who said she stays forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: לימא שמואל ורב אסי דאמרי כרבי אלעזר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the proof about רבי אלעזר from Step 19 to ask about שמואל and רב אסי's view from Step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Are שמואל and רב אסי just following רבי אלעזר, against the חכמים?

steps.title: Even the Rabbis would agree in this case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the claim that שמואל and רב אסי must follow רבי אלעזר. רבנן argue with him only in a case where the ban ended before she fell to the יבם. Here the ban started after she fell, so even רבנן agree she stays forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can even say they follow רבנן. רבנן argue with רבי אלעזר only where, from the moment she fell to the יבמים and on, she was not forbidden to them. But here, where she became forbidden after that, even רבנן agree.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on Step 20. שמואל and רב אסי do not need to follow רבי אלעזר alone. Even רבנן could agree with them here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key question is timing. In the case where רבנן argue, the ban on her was already over by the time of נפילה, so it does not count. In our case she was fine at נפילה and then became forbidden when the יבם married her sister, and that ban sticks even according to רבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: You can even say (introduces a pushback)
The moment the husband dies and the widow 'falls' to the יבם
They only argue in a specific case

steps.whatToRemember: A ban that starts after נפילה keeps the יבמה forbidden even according to רבנן. A ban that ended before נפילה is the case where רבנן argue with רבי אלעזר.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבנן reject the idea of 'forbidden once, forbidden forever' completely. They only argue in a case where the ban was over before נפילה.
steps.whyThisMatters: Now שמואל and רב אסי no longer depend on a minority view. Their ruling can fit everyone's opinion.

phrases.english: You can even say they follow the Rabbis,
the Rabbis only disagree
with Rabbi Elazar
because from the time she fell to them and onward
phrases.notes: 'Fell' means the moment her husband died and she became tied to the יבמים.

phrases.english: she was not forbidden to them,
but here, where she became forbidden,
even the Rabbis agree.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא כְּרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects Step 20's suggestion that שמואל and רב אסי follow only רבי אלעזר.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that שמואל and רב אסי need רבי אלעזר's minority view.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The suggestion missed that רבנן argue only where the ban ended before נפילה, not where it started after נפילה.

steps.title: New משנה: three-month wait before remarrying
steps.stepSummary: A יבמה may not do חליצה or יבום until three months have passed. All other women must also wait three months before אירוסין or נישואין, whatever their status.
steps.simpleTranslation: A יבמה may not do חליצה or יבום until three months have passed. Likewise, all other women may not get engaged or married until three months have passed. This applies to virgins and non-virgins, divorcées and widows, women who were married and women who were only engaged.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It sets a three-month waiting period before a יבמה or any other woman can move on to a new man.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule covers everyone, even women for whom the worry hardly seems to apply, like a virgin or a woman who was only engaged. The usual reason, which the גמרא explains later, is to make sure it is clear who a baby's father is.

keyTerms.meaning: Get engaged (אירוסין, the first stage of marriage)
Women who were only engaged, not fully married

steps.whyThisMatters: This three-month wait is the starting point for the next סוגיא and for the practical הלכה of waiting before remarriage.

phrases.english: Mishnah:
The yevama may not perform chalitza
and may not enter into yibum
until she has three months.
phrases.notes: The three months are counted from her husband's death.

phrases.english: And similarly, all other women
may not be betrothed and may not marry
until they have three months:
both virgins and non-virgins,
both divorcées and widows,
both married women and betrothed women.
phrases.notes: He means women who had been fully married to the previous husband, and women who had only been engaged to him.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַיְּבָמָה לֹא תַּחֲלוֹץ וְלֹא תִּתְיַיבֵּם עַד שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהּ שְׁלֹשָׁה חֳדָשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Every יבמה and every woman whose marriage or engagement ended must wait three months before חליצה, יבום, אירוסין or נישואין.

steps.title: רבי יהודה's exceptions to the three-month wait
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says a woman who was married may get engaged right away, and a woman who was only engaged may get married right away. The exception is engaged women in יהודה, where the couple was close during the engagement.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: Women who were married may get engaged, and women who were only engaged may get married. The exception is engaged women in יהודה, because the groom is familiar with her.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה argues with the first opinion in the משנה. He allows some women to move forward without waiting the full three months.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Where there is no real worry, רבי יהודה does not require the wait. An engaged woman never lived with her husband, so she can even marry right away. A married woman may only get engaged, not married. Engaged couples in יהודה were close and might have been together, so for them the worry is real again.

keyTerms.meaning: The region of Judea, which had its own engagement customs
He is familiar and comfortable with her

steps.confusionAlert: 'הנשואות יתארסו' does not mean a formerly married woman may fully marry right away. She may only get engaged within the three months.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
The married women may be betrothed,
and the betrothed women may marry.
except for the betrothed women in Judea,
because he is familiar with her.
phrases.notes: Literally 'his heart is coarse with her.' He was comfortable around her, so they may have been together already.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: הַנְּשׂוּאוֹת יִתְאָרְסוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the first opinion in the משנה (Step 22) and allows exceptions.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Formerly married women may get engaged, and formerly engaged women may marry, without waiting. Engaged women in יהודה are the exception.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: every woman may get engaged, except a widow
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי says all women may get engaged during the three months, except a widow. The משנה continues with his reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: All women may get engaged, except a widow.
steps.whatsHappening: A third opinion in the משנה begins. רבי יוסי allows engagement during the waiting period for every woman except a widow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי goes further than רבי יהודה, letting all women get engaged within the three months. He singles out the widow as an exception. The reason comes in the next words of the משנה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:
All the women may be betrothed,
phrases.notes: He means even within the three months, and even women who had been fully married.

phrases.english: except for a widow,

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: כׇּל הַנָּשִׁים יִתְאָרְסוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third opinion, more lenient than רבי יהודה except for a widow.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All women may get engaged during the three months, except a widow.
